This report is an Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) report publicly disclosed by CSPC Pharmaceutical Group Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as "CSPC," "we," "the Group," or "the Company"). It aims to respond to stakeholder expectations and present the Company's philosophy, management approach, actions, and performance in environmental, social, corporate governance, and sustainable development.

section: About This Report
text: This report has been prepared in accordance with Appendix C2 "Environmental, Social and Governance Reporting Code" to the Rules Governing the Listing of Securities on The Main Board of the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited and the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)'s IFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information and the IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures . It also references the GRI Sustainability Reporting Standards issued by the Global Sustainability Standards Board (GSSB), as well as major ESG rating indices in the capital markets such as the MSCI ESG Ratings.

text: Talent is the Company's most valuable asset and the core engine of innovation-driven development. Upholding our talent philosophy of "valuing talent and capability, embracing diversity, and helping people succeed," we have built a career development system covering the entire employee life cycle. In 2025, women accounted for 48% of our workforce, while the proportion of women in the middle- and senior-management team rose to 59%, reflecting a stronger culture of diversity, equality, and inclusion. section: Chairman's Message
text: Innovation is embedded in CSPC's DNA and remains the core strength with which we respond to the demands of our time. Guided by our dual strategy of "innovation + internationalization," we continued to increase investment in R&D. In 2025, our R&D expenses reached RMB 5.809 billion, accounting for approximately 28.2% of revenue from finished drug business. The Group had more than 200 innovative drug and novel formulation projects under development. Supported by eight core technology platforms, including nanomedicine, ADC, and mRNA vaccines, we have not only further strengthened our presence in key therapeutic areas such as oncology, neurology and psychiatry, and cardiovascular diseases, but also continued to make progress in rare disease drug development. section: Board ESG Statement
text: The Company has established a sound ESG governance framework, forming a three-tier management structure comprising the "Board of Directors - ESG Professional Guidance Team - ESG Working Group," which provides organizational support for the orderly advancement of ESG management. As the highest decision-making body and governing body for ESG matters, the Board of Directors leads and assumes overall responsibility for the Company's environmental, social and governance work. Its main responsibilities include formulating ESG strategies and targets, reviewing assessments of material risks and opportunities, overseeing the response to and management of ESG-related risks and opportunities with a material impact on the Company's business, and reviewing ESG-specific policies and the ESG report. As the core management body for ESG work, Professional Guidance Team is responsible for assessing ESG-related risks and opportunities, coordinating resource allocation, reviewing ESG management matters and policies, and supervising the timely alignment of the Company's ESG policies with national requirements. The ESG Coordination Office serves as the executive body for ESG matters, coordinating and advancing the implementation of ESG-related work across departments. In addition, the Company has established an ESG Working Group and subsidiary-level ESG Working Groups, which are responsible for implementing annual ESG work plans, participating in the formulation of ESG targets and the preparation of the ESG report, and collaboratively advancing specific ESG initiatives.

text: Guided by the philosophy of "All for Good Medicine, All for Mankind's Health," CSPC Pharmaceutical Group Limited has grown through innovation into an international and innovation-driven enterprise with a workforce of 20,000 employees. The Company (Stock code: 01093.HK) was listed on the Main Board of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited in 1994 and was included as a constituent of the Hang Seng Index in 2018. Guided by the philosophy of "All for Good Medicine, All for Mankind's Health," CSPC Pharmaceutical Group Limited has grown through innovation into an international and innovation-driven enterprise with a workforce of 20,000 employees. section: Company Profile
text: Through innovation on a global scale, we continuously deliver better healthcare solutions for humanity. With five major global R&D centers and a high-caliber R&D team of more than 2,000 professionals, we are advancing research into new technologies, new targets, and new frontiers, with a focus on key treatment areas including oncology, neuroscience, cardiovascular, immunology and respiratory, gastrointestinal and metabolic, and anti-infectives. We have established a diversified product portfolio spanning three major business segments: finished drugs, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and functional foods. Supported by eight technology platforms, including nanomedicine, mRNA, and ADC, CSPC is focused on six core therapeutic areas: oncology, neurology and psychiatry, cardiovascular, immunology and respiratory, metabolism, and anti-infectives. The Group currently has more than 200 innovative drug candidates in development, including over 90 macromolecular drugs, more than 60 small molecule drugs, and over 50 novel formulations.

text:
Background Analysis and Preliminary Topic Identification | • Analyze the Group's business model, operational characteristics, industry environment, and major stakeholder groups to define the background and boundaries of the assessment.
Establishment of the Preliminary Topic List | • Integrate industry benchmarking, regulatory guidance, international standards, and the Group's own operational realities to screen, consolidate, and refine topics, forming a comprehensive preliminary pool of topics.
Double Materiality Assessment | • Impact Materiality Assessment: The Group evaluates the impact materiality of each topic across three dimensions. The first is likelihood of risk exposure, namely the probability that the topic may have a negative impact on the Group. The second is severity, referring to the potential extent of damage if the impact occurs. The third is risk adaptation capacity, meaning the effectiveness of the Group's existing control systems in responding to the risk. Based on the analysis of these dimensions, a conclusion is reached regarding the impact materiality of each topic. • Financial Materiality Assessment: We adopted an expert assessment approach and organized the heads of the Finance Department and other relevant departments to evaluate the potential multi-dimensional impacts of each ESG topic on the Group's revenue, costs, assets, and valuation. We also analyzed the pathways and potential scale of these impacts on the Group's financial performance over the short, medium, and long term. Based on this multi-stage assessment, each topic was assigned an overall financial materiality score, and the final rating was determined according to pre-set thresholds.
Integrated Analysis and Topic Confirmation | • Integrate the results of the impact materiality and financial materiality assessments to identify the double materiality topics that are of major significance to the Group's sustainable development.
Review, Reporting and Disclosure | • The assessment process, methodology, and materiality matrix are submitted to the Board for review and confirmation before public disclosure.

section: 1.1.2 Board Composition / 1.1 Corporate Governance
text: The Group regards the independent non-executive director system as a core component of a sound corporate governance framework. In managing board independence, the Group applies strict standards and requires independent non-executive directors to maintain an independent position and provide objective views in performing their oversight duties. In the selection and appointment process, the Group places particular emphasis on reviewing the independence of candidates' identities and relationships to ensure that independent non-executive directors can effectively perform their duties, enhancing the Board's supervisory effectiveness and decision-making quality and improving the fairness and transparency of corporate governance.

section: 1.1.2 Board Composition / 1.1 Corporate Governance
text: As the Group's decision-making body, the Board of Directors is responsible for setting strategic directions, establishing objectives and business plans, and overseeing financial and operational performance. The Board performs its duties in strict accordance with the Group's governance requirements, and the procedures for convening, holding, and voting at Board meetings are all in compliance with relevant regulations. The Board has established 3 specialized committees under its authority: the Remuneration Committee, the Nomination Committee, and the Audit Committee. Each committee performs its duties in strict accordance with applicable requirements, providing strong support for the professionalism and efficiency of the Board's deliberations and decision-making. In 2025, the Group had a total of 17 directors, and Board attendance reached 100%.

Each committee performs its duties in strict accordance with applicable requirements, providing strong support for the professionalism and efficiency of the Board's deliberations and decision-making. In 2025, the Group had a total of 17 directors, and Board attendance reached 100%.

text: To regulate supplier conduct and foster a clean business environment, the Group has established the Tender Supervision and Management System and the Dishonest Blacklist Management System, requiring suppliers to sign the Sunshine Cooperation Agreement before participating in tendering activities. section: 1.3.2 Building a Culture of Integrity / 1.3.3 Anti-Unfair Competition
text: CSPC actively participates in establishing and maintaining a fair and orderly market environment, and works to prevent and combat monopolistic conduct, abuse of market dominance, and improper concentration of undertakings. The Group strictly complies with the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, the Anti-monopoly Guidelines in the Field of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients , and other applicable laws and regulations. On this basis, we have established internal management policies such as the Dishonest Blacklist Management System, which clearly defines 15 categories of unfair competition conduct. Where a business partner is found, upon investigation, to have engaged in non-compliant conduct, the Group will disclose the matter internally in accordance with its policies and place the party on the dishonest blacklist. From the effective date of such blacklisting, the partner will be prohibited from participating in any tendering projects of the Group, and all direct and indirect business dealings with the Group will be fully terminated. In 2025, the Group was not involved in any litigation or material administrative penalties arising from unfair competition conduct.

section: Quality Management System / Quality Audits
text: CSPC continues to supervise, inspect, and guide its subsidiaries through a normalized internal audit mechanism. In 2025, the Group formed dedicated inspection teams by selecting professional inspectors from its internal inspector pool to carry out in-depth quality system inspections and special crosschecks among subsidiaries. During the year, a total of 37 system, unannounced, and special inspections were completed. Through these internal audits, communication and the sharing of advanced quality management practices and typical issues identified in both internal and external inspections were further strengthened across subsidiaries.

section: Quality Management System / Quality Audits
text: The Group rigorously fulfills its primary responsibility for drug quality and safety by formulating and implementing the Quality Responsibility Management System , under which the safety responsibilities of drug marketing authorization holders and food manufacturers and operators are clearly embedded across all management dimensions. Through a cross-functional quality coordination mechanism, we have established a matrix of responsibilities and accountabilities covering the full product life cycle and the entire value chain, ensuring that quality responsibilities at every stage are performed with precision. In addition, the Group relies on a four-level quality assurance system comprising the Group, company, department, and team levels. Supported by a professional quality management team and refined vertical management, this system enables comprehensive and in-depth oversight of quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA) across the Group's member enterprises.

The Group rigorously fulfills its primary responsibility for drug quality and safety by formulating and implementing the Quality Responsibility Management System , under which the safety responsibilities of drug marketing authorization holders and food manufacturers and operators are clearly embedded across all management dimensions. Through a cross-functional quality coordination mechanism, we have established a matrix of responsibilities and accountabilities covering the full product life cycle and the entire value chain, ensuring that quality responsibilities at every stage are performed with precision. In addition, the Group relies on a four-level quality assurance system comprising the Group, company, department, and team levels. Supported by a professional quality management team and refined vertical management, this system enables comprehensive and in-depth oversight of quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA) across the Group's member enterprises.

section: Quality Management System / Quality Audits
text: The Group actively aligns itself with major global regulatory standards and continues to validate the compliance and internationalization of its quality system through external audits and authoritative certifications. All subsidiaries operate in strict accordance with China's GMP requirements and continue to improve production quality management with international standards as the benchmark. As of the end of the reporting period, the Group held a cumulative total of 15 CEP certificates, 15 ANDA products, and 1 NDA product. Relevant active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) and formulation enterprises manage their quality systems in accordance with ICH Q7, U.S. cGMP, and EU GMP requirements. All pharmaceutical production lines of the Group have passed GMP certification. During the reporting period, the Group underwent 62 inspections by domestic and international drug regulatory authorities, all of which were successfully passed.

In accordance with internationally recognized ICH guidelines and the relevant requirements of the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), the Group has established and continues to refine a Clinical Quality Management System (cQMS) covering the entire clinical trial process. In 2025, guided by the core principle that "quality built by design, and responsibility runs throughout the process," the Company worked to elevate quality management from a single focus on compliance inspection to a strategic capability that drives R&D efficiency and sustainable development, building a dynamic management system covering the full value chain and highly responsive to regulatory trends. During the year, the Group continued to optimize and improve its policies and procedures, revising and refining more than 20 SOPs, work manuals, and templates to ensure that the quality management system remained closely aligned with the latest domestic and international regulations, including ICH GCP E6 (R3), as well as the Group's own organizational structure.

section: Table: Certification and GMP Compliance of Formulation Companies / Certification Status
text: The Group implements a front-loaded risk management approach, moving the starting point of quality management significantly forward to the clinical trial project initiation and protocol design stages. Potential risks are assessed based on multiple dimensions, including historical audit data, site qualifications, researcher experience, and national inspection findings. Through the establishment of a clinical key document review mechanism and the strengthening of upfront resource allocation, systemic risks are mitigated at the source. The Group adopts a combined management model of routine monitoring and risk-based oversight, using centralized statistical monitoring to capture abnormal signals in key indicators such as enrollment pace, data query rates, and protocol deviations in real time. This enables monitoring and quality control resources to focus on the most critical data and processes, ensuring the compliance of trial conduct and the authenticity of results.

section: Table: Certification and GMP Compliance of Formulation Companies / Certification Status
text: The Group's quality management system for preclinical pharmaceutical research deeply integrates foundational management with risk management, with the aim of ensuring the steady advancement of pharmaceutical R&D. On the foundational management side, we have established a multi-dimensional management framework covering quality, materials, equipment, and laboratory management. Through refined control over pilot production, analytical method development, reference standards management, and electronic data management, together with risk control measures for deviations and changes, we have enabled effective integration between pharmaceutical R&D and subsequent manufacturing. On the risk management side, we have adopted the ICH Q10 quality risk management concept, covering the full lifecycle from drug development to pre-launch. By identifying and assessing compliance risks at critical research stages, and through closed-loop management of deviations and quality feedback, we ensure that risks are effectively controlled before project submission. Since 2018, the Group has undergone on-site inspections for pharmaceutical development for a cumulative total of 16 projects, all of which were successfully passed, including 2 FDA registration inspection projects, 4 inspections by the National Medical Products Administration, and 10 inspections by provincial drug regulatory authorities. Looking ahead, we will continue to deepen both foundational and risk management and further enhance the effectiveness of our R&D quality system.

CSPC is committed to integrating technological innovation with institutional development, deeply combining advanced manufacturing equipment with intelligent information systems to build a high-quality manufacturing system covering the entire value chain from materials and production to product release.

section: 2.1.3 Manufacturing Quality Management
text: The application of advanced production equipment and information tools such as MES, WMS, LIMS, and traceability systems provides the core driving force for the Group's smart manufacturing. In terms of software management, subsidiaries across the Group have established rigorous production and process control systems and operating procedures aimed at standardizing employee operations, effectively preventing mix-ups and errors, and minimizing the risks of contamination and cross-contamination. After receiving materials, production workshops carry out manufacturing strictly in accordance with process requirements and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for each position. Once finished product sampling is completed, products are transferred to the warehouse pending inspection and are subject to strict control by the quality management department. The QC laboratories fully apply the LIMS system for automated data management, effectively reducing human error. In addition, critical production areas' pressure differentials and temperature/humidity levels, warehouse temperature and humidity, laboratory refrigerator temperatures, and stability chamber temperature and humidity are all equipped with automatic monitoring and alarm systems. Through an early warning mechanism triggered whenever parameters exceed limits, delays caused by human judgment are reduced. Each batch of product is assigned a unique batch number, ensuring a full-process and traceable quality closed loop throughout the product life cycle.

text: All subsidiaries of the Group have established comprehensive quality management systems covering six core systems of pharmaceutical manufacturing and operations. Each subsidiary has also put in place mechanisms for tracking laws, regulations, and standards, enabling the timely follow-up of the latest compliance requirements issued both domestically and internationally, and their accurate translation into internal management systems. Each company has established full-process management systems covering material receipt, production control, finished product release, and distribution. On the hardware side, production workshops are designed and constructed in strict accordance with the standards of smart manufacturing and internationalization, reaching internationally leading levels. In accordance with the relevant requirements of ICH Q9 on quality risk management, we have established a sound risk control framework and a Quality Risk Management System to comprehensively identify risk points that may affect product quality throughout the product life cycle. During the risk assessment process, the quality management department organizes expert teams to use professional assessment tools such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), factor analysis, and fishbone diagrams to assess risks across different products and processes, and implements graded management based on the results.

The Group has dedicated pre-marketing and post-marketing pharmacovigilance teams and has built a pharmacovigilance system covering the entire product life cycle, while overseeing the effective operation of the system across all formulation companies. The Group has established a Drug Safety Committee responsible for handling major drug safety incidents at the Group level, while each formulation company is responsible for executing its company-level system and has clearly defined and continuously improved the processes for collecting, reporting, and handling adverse drug reactions. Each member enterprise is equipped with dedicated personnel commensurate with its production scale to ensure the effective implementation of management systems.

section: Pharmaceutical Quality and Safety Traceability
text: In terms of system standardization, in accordance with the requirements of the Good Pharmacovigilance Practice (GVP), the Administrative Measures for Adverse Drug Reaction Reporting and Monitoring, and other relevant regulations, the Group has established 87 management procedures, policies, and guidance documents. These include the Pharmacovigilance Management System, Emergency Response Plan for Major Adverse Drug Reaction Events, Drug Safety Committee Management System, Internal Audit Management System for the Pharmacovigilance System, Pharmacovigilance Database Management System, and Standard Operating Procedures for Drug Safety Information Collection. Of these, 53 documents were developed by the pre-marketing pharmacovigilance team and 34 by the post-marketing pharmacovigilance team, covering key areas such as individual case safety report handling, literature searches, Development Safety Update Reports (DSURs), Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRERs), signal detection, and risk management.

section: Product Recalls
text: The Group has developed a comprehensive pharmacovigilance plan and implements continuous monitoring measures. In terms of system operation, the Group has established a multi-channel information collection network. Dedicated personnel conduct real-time monitoring and collection through channels including the national direct adverse reaction reporting system, dedicated email addresses, clinical studies, market programs, academic literature, and relevant websites and forums. Supported by its pharmacovigilance information system, the Group processes, evaluates, and reports individual suspected adverse reaction cases to ensure that, in the event of cluster or major adverse reaction incidents, emergency measures can be launched promptly and relevant national and local regulatory authorities can be notified in a timely manner. In addition, each formulation company under the Group submits its annual pharmacovigilance report and periodic drug safety reports on schedule every year, using data-driven approaches to strengthen safety management and fully protect patient medication safety. In 2025, the Group did not receive any reports of cluster adverse reaction incidents caused by product defects.

section: Product Recalls
text: To address the recall of defective products, each subsidiary of the Group has formulated and implemented a Product Recall Management System, clearly defining the respective responsibilities of relevant departments such as quality and sales, and establishing standardized product recall procedures. In strict accordance with the severity of potential drug safety risks, the Group classifies recalls into Class I, Class II, and Class III to ensure a precise risk response. At the same time, the quality management departments of each company regularly organize mock recall drills to continuously verify and ensure the effective operation of the recall system. In 2025, no recalls were recorded for any products sold or delivered by the Group due to safety or health reasons.

section: Product Recalls
text: The Group has established a Quality Information Management System, which sets out the procedures for handling information related to counterfeit drugs and infringement. A dedicated rights protection task force has been set up to define follow-up actions, as well as the responsibilities and division of work among departments, based on the level of impact and urgency of counterfeit or infringement cases. Where necessary, the Legal Affairs Center and the Patent and Government Affairs Department will initiate relevant legal proceedings. The rights protection task force follows up on the progress of each case until it has been fully resolved. Within one week after the conclusion of each case, a summary report is prepared, and corresponding follow-up preventive measures are formulated to standardize handling procedures and prevent similar issues from recurring. Where counterfeit or infringement incidents give rise to reputational risks, they are handled in accordance with the General Rules for Media Crisis Emergency Response of CSPC Pharmaceutical Group.

text: The Group has established a comprehensive quality management training system covering the full process from training needs assessment and analysis to planning and implementation. Each subsidiary formulates an annual training plan and is explicitly required to include specialized training on quality management knowledge and GMP-related content relevant to job responsibilities. This ensures that all employees receive effective training when joining the Company, during their regular employment, and when transferring to new positions, so that they possess the qualifications and skills required for their roles and thereby strengthen the quality foundation from a human resources perspective. In 2025, the Group organized a total of 708 quality system training sessions, achieved 100% employee coverage for quality training, and recorded an average of 92 training hours per employee.

section: 2.2.1.4 R&D Training / 2.2.2.1 Intellectual Property Protection and Risk Management
text: Guided by the management policy of "encouraging innovation, controlling risks, effectively utilizing intellectual property, and enhancing the Group's core competitiveness and strategic advantage in IP," the Group has established a patent protection system suited to its operations and new-drug R&D activities. We protect core R&D achievements from multiple angles and in a comprehensive manner, and we have formulated robust patent filing, protection, and risk-avoidance strategies for key products. In generic drug development, the Group flexibly uses patent design-around strategies, patent challenges, and patent licensing to address market-launch compliance issues. The Group has also established a full-cycle patent early-warning analysis and risk-control mechanism covering the entire period from project initiation to product launch. It conducts regular diagnostic analyses so that, while avoiding infringement risks, it can also make appropriate use of legal means to safeguard the Group's lawful rights and interests. In 2025, the Group obtained recertification of its intellectual property management system and has now successfully passed seven on-site certification audits in total.

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: CSPC regards "participants' rights first, ethics before science" as an unwavering core principle in clinical R&D, making it explicit that under all circumstances, the protection of participants' dignity, safety, rights, and well-being takes precedence over scientific exploration and social benefit. Every clinical study we conduct strictly follows international and domestic ethical and quality standards, including but not limited to the World Medical Association Declaration of Helsinki, ICH GCP, the Good Clinical Practice for Pharmaceutical Products (GCP 2020), the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the Vaccine Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Measures for the Administration of Drug Registration. Meanwhile, the Group fulfills its corporate responsibilities by strictly implementing the requirements on ethical submission and reporting set out in ICH GCP E6(R3), the CIOMS Guidelines, and the Measures for the Ethical Review of Life Science and Medical Research Involving Humans, ensuring that research is conducted within a compliant, scientific, and ethical framework.

We strictly comply with national and local laws and regulations, including the National Standards for the Environment and Facilities for Laboratory Animals of the People's Republic of China, the Guidelines for the Ethical Review of Laboratory Animal Welfare of the People's Republic of China, the Measures for the Administration of Laboratory Animals of Hebei Province , and the Regulations on the Administration of Laboratory Animals, to ensure that animal experiments are lawful and compliant.

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: The Group's ethics governance covers the full life cycle of clinical research, including study design, execution, oversight, and closeout. At the protocol design stage, we communicate with ethics committees in advance and solicit views on key ethical issues so that study protocols better reflect best ethical principles. Before any study begins, it must be reviewed and approved by an independent ethics committee (IEC/IRB), and participants' right to be informed is fully protected throughout implementation. We explain the study objectives, methods, possible risks, and potential benefits to participants in detail, ensuring that they voluntarily sign informed consent forms on the basis of a full understanding of the relevant information. If protocol amendments occur during the study, or if any new information arises that could affect a participant's decision to continue, the Group promptly reports the matter to the ethics committee and communicates it to participants simultaneously, ensuring that they remain fully informed on an ongoing basis.

section: · Qualification requirements / 2.4.1.4 Supplier Risk Management
text: The Group conducts systematic risk identification at the admission stage, focusing on financial stability, production and supply capability, quality and process standards, and industry reputation. The Group has formulated the Supplier Management Policy, which stipulates that, in principle, the number of suppliers for raw and auxiliary materials shall be limited to two to three in order to ensure supply stability. In the event that there is only a single supplier, the Group will initiate the onboarding process for an additional supplier in accordance with the Change Management Policy and the Supplier Management Policy, carry out the corresponding quality studies, and, after completing the required filing procedures with the drug regulatory authorities in compliance with applicable regulations, include the supplier in the list of qualified suppliers, thereby eliminating the risks associated with reliance on a single supplier.

In terms of quality monitoring and audit certification, the Group has established a comprehensive audit system covering multiple tiers of the supply chain. This system covers not only most Tier-1 suppliers that directly provide products and services, but also extends to selected Tier-2 suppliers in order to strengthen whole-chain quality control. For upstream Tier-3 suppliers (raw materials), the Group regularly conducts stringent quality inspections and supervisory assessments of incoming raw materials and core components, and sets key indicators such as first-pass incoming acceptance rate and procurement factor deviation.For suppliers with potential risks in materials and quality, we initiate prompt communication to identify specific risk factors and key risk areas, and provide relevant training.

section: 2.4.2.3 Supplier Quality Management / 2.4.2.5 Equal Treatment of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
text:
Stage | Measure
Supplier Admission Stage | Using registered capital, revenue, and similar indicators as hard admission criteria is prohibited. The supplier comparison survey form was updated to increase the weighting of price advantage, supply capability, quality, and R&D capability, thereby reducing the weight of size-related factors at the admission stage.
Bidding Process | The digital platform (SRM system) conceals supplier size information and displays only key basic information such as qualifications, ensuring that evaluation focuses on supply capability and cost performance and enabling fair participation by SMEs.
Routine Management | The Group regularly surveys certain SMEs to collect information on obstacles encountered during bidding and optimizes procurement system message prompts and interface design based on the feedback. Through case analysis, regular training, and the sharing of selected company quality management standards, it guides and supports SMEs in strengthening compliance capability and quality and R&D capability. For some suppliers, one-to-one assistance is provided to interpret the Company's ESG requirements, discuss emissions reduction plans, and track progress in reducing emissions, ensuring that they meet the Company's requirements and standards.

section: 2.4.2.3 Supplier Quality Management / 2.4.2.5 Equal Treatment of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
text: The Group has formulated and implemented the Management System for the Blacklist of Dishonest Parties, continuously monitors supplier compliance performance, and conducts annual anti-corruption audits of key material suppliers and major suppliers. section: Table: Supplier Environmental Assessment Index / Case Study: Yinhu Selected as a National Green Factory
text:
Type | Specific Measures
Project Compliance Control | • Project siting strictly complies with ecological red-line requirements and other planning requirements, and projects are prohibited from being located in nature reserves and other sensitive areas. Chemical active pharmaceutical ingredient projects are all located in compliant industrial parks.
Ecological Survey and Protection | • During early planning, native vegetation, water sources, and key species habitats are identified and protected. During construction, measures such as tree transplantation and buffer zones are adopted.
Enriching Site Greening | • Site greening adopts a multi-layer configuration of trees, shrubs, and herbaceous plants, with multiple plant species used to create a diverse ecological environment.
Sustainable Maintenance | • Professional teams are engaged to carry out eco-friendly maintenance; soil monitoring is conducted annually; and ecological emergency plans for extreme weather and other events are developed.
Pollution Control | • Strict treatment measures are adopted for waste gas, wastewater, noise, and solid waste generated by projects to ensure compliant discharge.

section: 3.3.1.2 Energy Management Measures / 3.3 Resource Conservation
text: CSPC adheres to a green development philosophy and systematically promotes energy conservation, consumption reduction, and efficient resource utilization. By establishing an energy management system, building an intelligent energy management center, and increasing the proportion of green electricity used, the Group continues to optimize its energy structure. Meanwhile, it actively implements water-saving upgrades and recycling, and strengthens full-process control over packaging-material use, thereby improving resource efficiency and supporting the Company's green and low-carbon transformation.

section: 3.3.1.2 Energy Management Measures / 3.3 Resource Conservation
text:
Type of Measures | Specific Measures
Process Optimization | • Improvements to refined solution preparation equipment. Modification of the influent water supply mode for the micro-oxygen system. Optimization of purified-water system parameters. Recovery of residual heat from rectification for use in concentration processes.
Equipment Upgrades | • Replacement of pumps with energy-efficient models. Installation of thermo- compression distilled-water units to replace multi-effect distilled-water units. Replacement of coal-fired boilers with natural-gas boilers.
System Retrofits | • Interconnection retrofit of the compressed-air system. Addition of phase-change energy savers to the air-conditioning system. Economical operation of refrigeration systems. Combined operation of utility systems.
Management Optimization | • Introduction of direct power-purchase transactions. Improvement of the power factor. Optimization of air-conditioning operation and temperature control.

section: 4.1 Talent Attraction / Case Study: "Taima Business War" Simulation Training Promotes Diverse Communication and Exchange
text: We firmly believe that a diverse, equitable, and inclusive team is a core driver of innovation and sustainable development. Accordingly, we have established the CSPC Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Policy. In talent recruitment and selection, we strictly follow the principle of non-discrimination and do not differentiate among candidates on the basis of education, religion, nationality, work background, marital status, gender, ethnicity, or race. During the initial résumé-screening stage, we also implement an anonymized screening mechanism that removes personal information such as ethnicity, ensuring that evaluation focuses on individual capability and potential. In internal promotion and compensation systems, we strictly prohibit any discrimination based on gender, age, or race. Diversity Target: By 2025, maintain a proportion of women in mid- to seniormanagement positions of no less than 40%.

section: 4.1 Talent Attraction / Case Study: "Taima Business War" Simulation Training Promotes Diverse Communication and Exchange
text: To deepen the concept of diversity, we organized diversity-themed training across multiple organizational systems, aiming to break down professional silos and strengthen cross-department collaboration. For example, in the "Taima Business War"simulation training for senior managers, management personnel from R&D, production, marketing, and functional departments were mixed into teams to jointly address complex challenges involving market competition, product development, and operations management. Through scenario-based simulation, participants from different functions gained a deeper understanding of one another's responsibilities and needs, effectively enhancing mutual trust and collaborative efficiency, and laying a practical foundation for stronger overall organizational collaboration.

[Content]
To deepen the concept of diversity, we organized diversity-themed training across multiple organizational systems, aiming to break down professional silos and strengthen cross-department collaboration. For example, in the "Taima Business War"simulation training for senior managers, management personnel from R&D, production, marketing, and functional departments were mixed into teams to jointly address complex challenges involving market competition, product development, and operations management. Through scenario-based simulation, participants from different functions gained a deeper understanding of one another's responsibilities and needs, effectively enhancing mutual trust and collaborative efficiency, and laying a practical foundation for stronger overall organizational collaboration.

section: 4.1.3.3 Consultation and Complaints
text:
Employee | • Employees submit inquiries or complaint feedback through the "I Want to Consult" module in the shared services portal. • For inquiries, employees may consult online by selecting a question category and a specific question, or they may transfer to manual input and enter the question directly. • For complaints and feedback, employees select the feedback type and enter the specific issue.
Function/ Segment Leaders | • When the system receives an employee inquiry, it automatically assigns a responder, who must respond and address the issue within two days. • When the system receives an employee complaint or feedback submission, the operations lead handles it based on the reported content. • Depending on the type and substance of the complaint, cases are divided into two categories: direct resolution and coordinated resolution. • For directly resolvable matters, the relevant responsible person may be assigned to reply. For matters requiring coordination, the next step is to contact the HR function of the employee's company for coordinated resolution.
BP (business partner) at Each Subsidiary | • The subsidiary BP (business partner) verifies the employee's feedback, coordinates resolution, and proposes a handling plan.
Operations Lead | • The operations lead informs the BP (business partner) of the relevant subsidiary about the employee's feedback and communicates with them. • Track handling progress in a timely manner. • Communicate with the subsidiary BP (business partner) and reach agreement on the final solution. • Reply through the employee feedback response interface in the EHR system. • Analyze employee inquiries and consider incorporating frequently asked questions into the knowledge base and HR handbook.

section: 4.1.3.3 Consultation and Complaints
text: To build an efficient and transparent internal communication mechanism, we officially launched the "Employee Self-Service Q&A" module in the EHR system, using digital tools to create an intelligent platform that integrates knowledge-base management, inquiry handling, and feedback follow-up. The platform enables 100% closed-loop resolution of employee inquiries. Based on high-frequency inquiry needs, we sorted and built 41 standard FAQ entries, established a keyword-based automatic matching and instant response mechanism, and improved inquiry handling efficiency. For issues not already covered, the system automatically routes the case to the appropriate responsible person based on the employee's business unit, ensuring precise assignment and timely response. In 2025, the platform handled 64 employee inquiries, all of which received effective feedback and resolution. We also review inquiry data regularly, synchronize high-frequency issues into the knowledge base, and continuously optimize service content to help employees obtain information efficiently and create a smoother, more convenient internal communication environment.

The platform enables 100% closed-loop resolution of employee inquiries. Based on high-frequency inquiry needs, we sorted and built 41 standard FAQ entries, established a keyword-based automatic matching and instant response mechanism, and improved inquiry handling efficiency. For issues not already covered, the system automatically routes the case to the appropriate responsible person based on the employee's business unit, ensuring precise assignment and timely response. In 2025, the platform handled 64 employee inquiries, all of which received effective feedback and resolution. We also review inquiry data regularly, synchronize high-frequency issues into the knowledge base, and continuously optimize service content to help employees obtain information efficiently and create a smoother, more convenient internal communication environment.

Social Recruitment | • We continuously post job openings on mainstream recruitment platforms such as 51job, Zhaopin, and Liepin to ensure fair access to information, reach experienced professionals, and meet our immediate demand for mature talent.

Internal Competition | • In accordance with the Internal Competition Management Measures, we open internal opportunities for competitive selection, providing current employees with clear career paths and lateral mobility opportunities, prioritizing internal selection, and invigorating the organization.
New Media Platforms | • We actively operate official new media channels such as CSPC Recruitment Online, releasing job information and showcasing corporate culture and employee stories in a more vivid and direct way to attract the attention of younger generations and passive job seekers.

To foster coordinated growth between talent and the organization, we have built a diversified and multidimensional internal development platform. We design development paths for cross-functional talent, create secondment programs, advance succession planning for key roles, and implement rotational mechanisms for mid-level managers, thereby activating employee potential, broadening career paths, and ensuring fair growth opportunities and broad development space for all categories of talent within the Group.

section: Case Study: "Shiyao Camp" -Campus Recruitment Reserve Talent Program
text: To cultivate young reserve talent, we designed the "Shiyao Camp" reserve program specifically for new hires graduating in 2025 across R&D, production, marketing, and functional systems. The program includes a dedicated onboarding curriculum centered on cultural integration and career growth, helping reserve trainees smoothly complete the transition from campus to the workplace and adapt to their new roles. After the centralized onboarding phase, we continue a one-year follow-up development program that combines online and offline methods, closely tracks rotational practice and mentor coaching, and incorporates two rounds of structured performance assessment to continuously unlock participants' growth potential and professional performance. This closed-loop development system helps reserve trainees adapt quickly and steadily build capability, while also supplying the organization with new talent that combines cultural alignment and job readiness, thereby improving both talent investment and development outcomes.

section: Case Study: Enterprise New Apprenticeship Training For the Development of Skilled Talent
text: To implement national requirements for building the industrial workforce, we systematically carried out the enterprise new apprenticeship training program. The program adopts a school-enterprise cooperation model combining work and study, with the aim of improving the professional quality and practical capabilities of skilled talent and strengthening the talent foundation for the Group's sustainable development. In 2025, CSPC organized a total of 1,352 newly hired and transferred frontline production employees in skilled roles from multiple subsidiaries, including Ouyi, Zhongnuo, CSPC NBP, CSPC Innovation, and CSPC Shengxue, to participate in the program. Using a deeply integrated 'theory plus practice' model, the program provided 160 class hours of theoretical learning and 240 class hours of on-the-job practical training, effectively improving participants' theoretical knowledge and vocational skills. After the program, 1,071 participants passed vocational skill level assessments and obtained national vocational skill certificates such as Senior Pharmaceutical Preparation Worker, Pharmaceutical Preparation Technician, and Senior Organic Synthesis Worker.

[Content]
To implement national requirements for building the industrial workforce, we systematically carried out the enterprise new apprenticeship training program. The program adopts a school-enterprise cooperation model combining work and study, with the aim of improving the professional quality and practical capabilities of skilled talent and strengthening the talent foundation for the Group's sustainable development. In 2025, CSPC organized a total of 1,352 newly hired and transferred frontline production employees in skilled roles from multiple subsidiaries, including Ouyi, Zhongnuo, CSPC NBP, CSPC Innovation, and CSPC Shengxue, to participate in the program. Using a deeply integrated 'theory plus practice' model, the program provided 160 class hours of theoretical learning and 240 class hours of on-the-job practical training, effectively improving participants' theoretical knowledge and vocational skills. After the program, 1,071 participants passed vocational skill level assessments and obtained national vocational skill certificates such as Senior Pharmaceutical Preparation Worker, Pharmaceutical Preparation Technician, and Senior Organic Synthesis Worker.

section: CSPC Occupational Health and Safety Management Targets / 4.3.3 Building a Safety Culture
text: In strict accordance with the Work Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and the Administrative Provisions on Safety Training for Production and Business Operation Entities, the Group has established and continuously improved the EHS Education and Training Management System and formulated and implemented an annual EHS Training Plan. Through a model that combines online learning, offline practical training, and position-specific drills, we provide comprehensive coverage of both fundamental safety knowledge and advanced professional skills. Leveraging the "Xuanxing" training platform, we provide online courses and video training and organize in-person training sessions, workplace safety knowledge competitions, and thematic lectures for safety personnel, thereby enhancing employees' safety awareness and emergency response capabilities. In addition, during Fire Safety Month, we organize company-wide emergency evacuation drills and conduct multiple on-site emergency response drills in critical areas such as confined spaces, hazardous chemicals, electric shock, mechanical injury, and special equipment, strengthening practical emergency response capabilities and reinforcing the foundation for safe production.

Leveraging the "Xuanxing" training platform, we provide online courses and video training and organize in-person training sessions, workplace safety knowledge competitions, and thematic lectures for safety personnel, thereby enhancing employees' safety awareness and emergency response capabilities. section: CSPC Occupational Health and Safety Management Targets / 4.3.3 Building a Safety Culture
text: To achieve these occupational health and safety objectives, the Group has advanced the implementation of the production safety accountability system by requiring all employees to sign safety responsibility statements and by incorporating safety performance into the evaluation system, thereby reinforcing accountability at every level. In addition, we have established a routine advancement mechanism consisting of quarterly meetings, weekly self-inspections, and special rectification actions. We also integrate internal and external supervision resources to carry out regular inspections and targeted supervisory reviews, improving the effectiveness of safety management.

text: In March 2025, CSPC's project "Key Technologies and Industrial Application of New Excipients for High-end Formulations" won the Second Prize of the 2024 China Industry-University-Research Cooperation Promotion Association Science and Technology Innovation Award (Innovation Achievement Award). The related achievements have already been successfully applied to key products such as butylphthalide and doxorubicin liposome.

In May 2025, during the "Nanshan Respiratory Health Forum," CSPC hosted a multidisciplinary symposium that brought together 26 leading respiratory experts from across China. The meeting focused on frontier fields such as lung cancer and severe asthma and highlighted the clinical value and evidence base of the Group's three innovative drugs-Haiyitan, Enyitan, and Yiluoda. text: In January 2026, CSPC and AstraZeneca signed a strategic R&D cooperation and licensing agreement for innovative long-acting peptide drugs. Relying on the Group's proprietary sustained-release delivery platform and peptide medicine discovery platform, the two parties will jointly advance the development of eight long-acting weight management and innovation projects including SYH2082. The Group will grant AstraZeneca exclusive global rights outside Greater China and has the right to receive an upfront payment of USD 1.2 billion, with total milestone payments of up to USD 17.3 billion plus double-digit sales royalties. This cooperation not only set a new industry record for overseas expansion, but also strongly validated the power of the Group's innovative technology platforms in driving its globalization strategy.

Through independent R&D and technological innovation, the Group now has nine products that have obtained orphan drug designation from the U.S. FDA. For marketed products, Narusobimab Injection and Nintedanib Ethanesulfonate Soft Capsules have been successfully approved for marketing, effectively filling treatment gaps in the relevant fields.

section: 5.2.3 Rare Disease Drug R&D and Investment
text:
Disease Area | Key Pipeline Project | Major 2025 Progress and Clinical Value
Rare Malignant Tumors | SYHA1813 (high-grade meningioma) | Phase I enrollment has been completed, and the data show clear antitumor activity. A randomized controlled Phase II study is currently underway, and a Phase III clinical communication submission was made in October 2025, with the potential to fill a global clinical gap.
Rare Malignant Tumors | Narusobimab (giant cell tumor of bone) | Phase III clinical study enrollment has been completed. Compared with imported drugs, it has a faster onset and more controllable quality, and it is expected to receive full approval in 2028 for adult and adolescent patients.
Ultra-Rare Tumors | Albumin-bound sirolimus (malignant perivascular epithelioid cell tumor) | The Phase Ib/III trial has shown outstanding efficacy and good safety. Phase III enrollment is basically complete, and an NDA submission for marketing is planned for early 2026.
Rare Malignant Tumors | SYS6090 (melanoma) | SYS6090 Injection is a recombinant fully human bifunctional fusion protein. It received clinical approval in China and the United States in March and April 2025, respectively, and will soon start Phase I/II studies for unresectable or metastatic melanoma.
Rare Malignant Tumors | SYHX2008 (neuroendocrine tumor) | A prefilled long-acting octreotide injection. Phase II results showed good efficacy. The CDE has agreed to a pivotal Phase III study for adjuvant treatment after surgery for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNET).
Respiratory System | SYH2059 / SYH9061 (pulmonary fibrosis) | SYH2059 tablets are in the MAD stage, the inhalation dry powder formulation is planned to file an IND by the end of 2025, and nintedanib inhalation (SYH9061) filed its first IND in October.

section: 5.2.3 Rare Disease Drug R&D and Investment
text:
Generic Medicine Sales | • The Group markets a variety of products in low- and middle-income countries to enhance patient access to medicines, including Amoxicillin Capsules, Ceftriaxone Sodium for Injection, Ampicillin Capsules, Procaine Benzylpenicillin Fortified Sodium for Injection, Benzylpenicillin Sodium for Injection, Meropenem for Injection, and Azithromycin Film-Coated Tablets.
Pharmaco- vigilance System Development | • The Group has established a comprehensive monitoring and reporting mechanism for adverse drug reactions (ADRs) overseas. When adverse reactions occur outside China, the Group collaborates with local agents and customers to report to the local regulatory authorities in accordance with local regulations, and simultaneously notifies other customers marketing the same batch of products to submit reports. For serious adverse reactions occurring overseas, the Group ensures reporting to the National Center for Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring within 15 days upon notification. If a drug is suspended from sale, use, or withdrawn from the market overseas due to adverse reactions, a written report will be submitted to the National Medical Products Administration and the National Center for Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring within 24 hours. All other adverse reaction information is incorporated into the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) system for medicines.
Medical Personnel Training | • The Group actively dispatches personnel to provide guidance to local medical staff, and regularly organizes experts to conduct on-site exchanges and training to continuously strengthen the local medication safety system. In 2025, the Group organized 9 exchanges between hospitals in China and Southeast Asian countries, introducing the advantages and administration methods of TNK to overseas physicians, and disseminating product information on NBP and TNK to experts in Southeast Asian countries.

section: 5.3 Social Welfare
text:
Disease Area | Key Pipeline Project | Major 2025 Progress and Clinical Value
Hematologic System | SYS6053 (hemophilia A) | A biosimilar of emicizumab. An IND application was submitted in 2025, aiming to break the price monopoly of imported drugs and improve the affordability of preventive treatment for hemophilia.
Central Nervous System | Mitoxantrone Hydrochloride Liposome (neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder) | Phase II clinical study in NMOSD has been completed. Preclinical data confirm lower toxicity than conventional mitoxantrone, offering the prospect of a safer option for highly disabling patients.
Autoimmune System | LNP-mRNA CAR-T (myasthenia gravis) | The world's second and China's first mRNA CAR-T cell therapy for MG. It is currently in clinical trials and is expected to offer patients with refractory MG a therapy with rapid onset and good safety.
Endocrine System | SYHX2008 (acromegaly) | A prefilled long-acting octreotide injection. Compared with microsphere formulations, exposure is 4-5 times higher. Phase III clinical communication was completed in November 2025, and patients can self-administer it, greatly facilitating long-term treatment.
Metabolic System | Hydroxocobalamin Hydrochloride (SYH9097) (MMA) | China's first high-concentration formulation (20 mg/mL) developed for methylmalonic acidemia. It is currently in Phase III clinical development and aims to solve the risks associated with overseas purchasing and the urgent clinical need for pediatric patients.

section: 5.3.4 Support for Patients with Major Illnesses / Case Study: "Medical Assistance for Patients in Difficult Circumstances" Program
text: Congenital heart diseases such as atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus, and pulmonary artery stenosis, as well as acquired heart diseases such as coronary heart disease, hypertensive heart disease, and rheumatic heart disease, pose severe challenges for many families in difficult circumstances. To alleviate this hardship, the Group officially launched the "Medical Assistance for Patients in Difficult Circumstances" program in 2024, aiming to sustain life and restore hope to every heart awaiting treatment. In 2025, the program spent RMB 947,200 , organized 30 patient support and care activities, assisted 90 patients in difficult circumstances, and contributed 1,290 volunteer service hours.

section: 董事會ESG聲明
text: 公司已建立完善的ESG治理體系,形成由「董事會-ESG 專業指導團隊-ESG工作小組」構 成的三級管理架構,為ESG管理工作的有序開展提供組織保障。董事會作為公司ESG工作的 最高決策機構和治理層,領導並負責公司的環境、社會及管治事項,主要工作內容包括制定 ESG 戰略、目標,審閱重大風險與機遇的評估結果,監督對公司業務具有重大影響的ESG相 關風險與機遇的應對和管理,審議ESG專項制度及ESG報告。專業指導團隊作為ESG工作的 核心管理層,負責評估ESG相關風險與機遇,協調資源配置,審閱ESG管理事項和制度,及 督導公司ESG政策即時跟進國家要求。ESG協同辦公室作為ESG事項的執行機構,統籌推進各部門ESG相關工作的落實。同時,公司設立ESG工作小組及子公司ESG工作小組,負責 ESG 年度工作計劃的執行,參與ESG目標制定及報告編制,並協同推進具體ESG事項。 公司董事會高度重視ESG重要性議題的識別與判定。2025年,公司基於「影響重要性」和 「財務重要性」兩個維度,按照「識別-調研-評估-確認」流程,對雙重重要性議題進行了 系統梳理及動態優化,更新完成2025年雙重重要性議題矩陣,並經董事會審議後進行披露。 本報告詳盡披露公司2025年ESG管理工作的進展與實施情況,並經專業指導團隊審議後,於

section: 1.1.2 董事會構成 / 1.1 公司治理
text: 本集團視獨立非執行董事制度為完善公司治理體系的核心環節。本集團在董事獨立性的管理上 遵循嚴格標準,明確要求獨立非執行董事在執行監督職能時保持獨立立場並提供客觀意見。在 獨立非執行董事的選任過程中,本集團重點審核候選人身份與關係的獨立性,確保獨立非執行 董事有效履職,切實提升董事會的監督效能與決策質量,提高公司治理的公正性與透明度。

section: 1.1.2 董事會構成 / 1.1 公司治理
text: 董事會作為本集團的決策機構,負責確立策略性方針、訂立目標及業務計劃以及監督財政及運 營表現。董事會嚴格按照集團規定履行職責,董事會會議的召集、召開、表決等程序均符合相 關規定的要求。董事會下設薪酬委員會、提名委員會、審核委員會等三個專門委員會,各專門 委員會嚴格按照規定履行職責,為董事會議事決策的專業和高效提供充分保障。2025年,本 集團共有17名董事,董事會出勤率達100%。

text: 本集團制定全週期風險管理,將ESG風險納入企業風險管理(ERM)體系,完善從風險識 別、風險評估、風險應對、問題解決、複盤總結、後續控制監督等各項風險管理工作流程,實 現風險管理閉環。我們採取「各職能部門(業務、運營、市場)-合規管理部門-監察審計部 門」三道防線合規風險防控機制,切實將風險管理工作落實到公司運營的各個環節中,幫助企 業降低經營風險、更好地應對外部環境的變化。

section: 1.2.2 合規管理
text: 本集團定期開展合規內外部審計工作,以監督各部門合規工作的實際執行情況,全面反映合規 管理現狀。集團依據《石藥集團內部審計程序規定》,在董事會審核委員會的指導下獨立開展工作,搭建審計體系、開展各類審計監督、推動整改追責及實施索賠挽損,全面覆蓋財務、管 理、工程、舞弊及專項審計等領域,以完善內控體系、防範經營風險。2025年,本集團內部 審計工作以完善制度體系為基礎,運用大數據分析優化風險評估,聚焦銷售與收款、採購與付 款、生產與倉儲等核心流程開展系統性審計,識別控制缺陷並提出改進建議,通過閉環跟蹤整 改與追責挽損,持續提升內控有效性與經營穩健性。

section: 供應商反貪腐管理 / 1.3 廉潔合規
text: 為規範供應商合作行為並構建廉潔營商環境,本集團制定《招標監督管理制度》及《失信黑名單 管理制度》,要求供應商在招標前簽署《陽光合作協議》,並在標準合同中設立廉潔交易條款, 使其具有法律約束力。同時,我們通過全鏈條供應商管理體系,對合作中商業道德表現進行持續 評估,並對違規供應商採取拉黑處理,以保障招投標過程的公平公正與合作關係的廉潔合規。 2025 年,本集團開展覆蓋供應商准入、招投標、合同簽訂、款項支付、驗收入庫全生命週期審 計工作,共組織供應商簽署陽光合作協議10,254份,覆蓋所有參與集團招標議標的供應商。

section: 截至報告期末，集團8家子公司已取得ISO 9001質量管理體系認證。
text: 本集團臨床前藥學研發質量管理體系深度融合將基礎管理與風險管理相結合,旨在保障藥學研 發的穩健推進。在基礎管理方面,我們構建了涵蓋質量、物料、設備及實驗管理在內的多維度 管理架構,通過對中試生產、分析方法建立、標準品(對照品)管理及電子數據管理等環節的 精細化管控,並配合偏差、變更等風險防控措施,實現了藥學研發與後期生產的有效銜接。在 風險管理方面,我們引入ICH Q10質量風險管理理念,覆蓋藥品從研製到上市前的全生命週 期;通過對關鍵研究階段合規風險的識別與評估,以及對偏差和質量反饋的閉環管理,確保 項目在申報前風險已得到有效控制。自2018年以來,本集團累計接受16個項目的藥學研製現場核查,均順利通過,其中包括2個FDA註冊核查項目、4個國家藥監局核查項目及10個 省藥監局核查項目。未來,我們將持續深化基礎與風險管理,不斷提升研發質量體系的運行 效能。

section: 2.1.3 生產質量管理
text: 先進的生產設備與MES、WMS、LIMS、追溯系統等信息化工具的應用,為集團智能製造 提供了核心驅動力。在軟件管理上,集團各子公司建立了嚴密的生產及過程控制制度與操 作規程,旨在規範員工操作,有效規避混淆與差錯,最大程度降低污染及交叉污染的風 險。生產車間接收物料後,嚴格按照工藝規程及崗位的標準操作程序(SOP)完成生產; 在成品取樣完成後,將產品轉入倉庫待驗,由質量管理部門嚴格把控。QC實驗室全面應 用LIMS 軟件進行數據自動化管理,有效減少人為失誤。此外,關鍵生產間的壓差及溫濕 度、倉庫溫濕度、實驗室冰箱溫度、穩定性箱溫濕度均配備了自動監測及報警系統,通過 超標即預警的機制,減少了人為判斷的滯後性。每批產品均分配唯一批號,確保了在產品 生命週期內實現全過程、可追溯的質量閉環。

text: 本集團以SAP系統為主線,輔以多項專業管理系統,通過信息化建設全面助力智能製造。各 公司均建立了覆蓋物料進廠、生產控制、成品出廠至流通環節的全鏈條管理制度,結合信息化 系統的應用,實現了產品全生命週期的有效管理與持續改進。硬件方面,生產車間嚴格按照 「智能製造」與「國際化」標準設計建設,處於國際領先水平。通過SAP系統升級項目,本 集團對製造中心從銷售計劃、生產計劃、採購需求到生產任務的全流程業務現狀進行了深度梳 理,並對MES、WMS、LIMS、APS 等周邊系統的功能與流程進行了端到端的標準化整合。在 此基礎上,本集團成功實現了由「按庫生產」向「按單管理」邏輯的轉變,顯著提升了管理 效能。

text: 本集團質量風險管理的理念為「預防為主、防控結合、動態管理」。根據ICH Q9質量風險管 理的相關要求,我們建立了健全的風險控制體系及《質量風險管理制度》,對藥品生命週期內 可能影響產品質量的風險點進行全方位識別。在風險評估過程中,質量管理部門組織專家團隊 使用失效模式影響分析、影響因素分析及魚刺圖等專業評估工具對各種藥品及工序進行風險評 估,並根據結果實行分級管理。

text: 在物料流轉環節,本集團嚴格執行《物料驗收、儲存、發放管理制度》,確保所有物料均從合 格供應商處採購,並嚴格按儲存要求分類存放。通過明顯的待檢、放行及不合格標識與安全隔 離措施,有效杜絕差錯風險。所有物料必須經質量管理部門檢驗合格並批准放行後,方可進入 生產環節。

section: 產品召回
text: 本集團制定了全面的藥物警戒計劃,實施持續的監測措施。在體系運行方面,集團建立了多渠 道的信息收集網絡,通過國家不良反應直接報告系統、專用郵箱、臨床研究、市場項目、學術 文獻及相關網站論壇等途徑,由專職人員進行實時監測與收集。依託藥物警戒信息化系統,集 團對收集到的疑似不良反應信息進行個例報告處理、評價與上報,確保在發生群體或重大不良 反應事件時,能迅速啟動應急措施並及時向國家及地方監管部門通報。此外,本集團各製劑公 司每年均按時上報藥物警戒年度報告及藥品定期安全性報告,以數據驅動安全管理,全力保障 患者用藥安全。2025年,本集團未收到因藥品缺陷導致群體不良反應事件的報告。

section: 2.1.5 質量文化建設 / 案例：2025 年質量月活動

納米製劑技術平台 | • 作為國際最大的納米藥物研發及產業化基地,已有鹽酸米托蒽醌脂質體、紫杉 醇(白蛋白結合型)等8項藥物成功上市。
ADC技術平台 | • 開發了自主知識產權的定點偶聯技術,已有Nectin4-ADC、Claudin18.2- ADC、ROR1-ADC實現海外授權,10個產品已進入或即將進入臨床階段。
抗體/融合蛋白技術平台 | • 已有納魯索拜單抗、恩朗蘇拜單抗等5個產品獲批上市,後續還有30項單 抗、雙抗、抗體融合蛋白在研。

section: 2.2.1.4 研發培訓 / 2.2.2.1 知識產權保護與風險管理
text: 本集團基於「激勵創新、防控風險、有效運用、提高優勢」的管理方針,建立了與自身經營及 新藥研發相適應的專利保護體系。我們對核心研發成果實施多角度、全方位的保護,並針對核 心產品制定完善的專利申請、保護及風險規避策略。在仿製藥開發領域,集團靈活運用專利規 避、專利挑戰、尋求專利許可等方式解決上市合規問題。同時,本集團建立起從項目立項至產 品上市全週期的專利預警分析和風險管控機制,定期進行診斷分析,在規避侵權風險的同時, 合理運用法律手段維護集團的合法權益。2025年,本集團取得企業知識產權管理體系再認證 證書,至今已累計通過7次認證現場審核。

section: 2.2.3.3 臨床試驗受試者安全與權益保護 / 2.2.3 臨床倫理
text: 本集團始終將受試者的安全和權益放在臨床研究的各個階段,並落實到每一位臨床人員的工作 中。我們要求員工對工作過程中接觸到的受試者隱私及敏感信息嚴格保密,嚴防信息洩露。為 應對可能出現的風險和意外情況,本集團為每一項臨床試驗購買足額保險,確保受試者權益得 到充分保障。我們將保護受試者的安全和福祉視為履行企業社會責任的生命線,通過構建完善 的安全保障機制,確保臨床研究全過程的安全性與倫理性。

section: 2.2.3.3 臨床試驗受試者安全與權益保護 / 2.2.3 臨床倫理
text: 石藥集團將「受試者權益至上,倫理先行於科學」作為臨床研發不可動搖的核心準則,明確在 任何情況下,保護受試者的尊嚴、安全、權益與福祉均優先於科學探索與社會獲益。我們每項 臨床研究均嚴格遵循國際和國內的倫理與質量規範,包括但不限於《世界醫學大會赫爾辛基宣 言》、ICH GCP、《藥物臨床試驗質量管理規範》(GCP 2020)以及《中華人民共和國民法 典》《中華人民共和國藥品管理法》《中華人民共和國疫苗管理法》《藥品註冊管理辦法》等 法律法規。同時,本集團切實落實企業責任,嚴格執行ICH GCP E6(R3)、CIOMS指南、《涉 及人的生命科學和醫學研究倫理審查辦法》等文件中關於倫理上報和報告的要求,確保研究在 合規、科學與倫理框架下開展。

text: 石藥集團秉持人與自然和諧相處的理念,致力於科學、合理、人道地使用實驗動物。我們嚴格 遵守《中華人民共和國實驗動物環境及設施國家標準》《中華人民共和國實驗動物福利倫理審 查指南》《河北省實驗動物管理辦法》《實驗動物管理條例》等各項國家及地方性法律法規, 確保動物實驗的合法合規。

section: 2.2.3.3 臨床試驗受試者安全與權益保護 / 2.2.3 臨床倫理
text: 本集團的倫理治理覆蓋臨床研究設計、執行、監管與結束的全生命週期。在方案設計階段,我 們即與倫理委員會進行前置溝通,就關鍵倫理議題徵詢意見,使研究方案更符合倫理最優原 則。所有研究啟動前均需通過獨立倫理委員會(IEC/IRB)的審核批准,並在實施過程中充分 保障參與者的知情權。我們向受試者詳細說明研究目的、方法、可能的風險與潛在益處,確保 其在充分了解信息的基礎上自願簽署知情同意書。若研究過程中發生方案修訂,或出現任何可 能影響受試者繼續參與研究決定的新信息,本集團會及時上報倫理委員會,並同步傳達給受試 者,確保其持續處於充分知情狀態。

section: 2.2.3.3 臨床試驗受試者安全與權益保護 / 2.2.3 臨床倫理
text: 本集團設立了實驗動物福利倫理委員會,制定並執行《實驗動物倫理福利管理規定》《實驗動 物倫理審查標準操作規程》等制度。我們建立了專業的飼養管理體系與獸醫保健團隊,保證實 驗動物享有基本權利,包括不受飢渴、生活舒適、不受痛苦傷害與疾病、無恐懼感以及表達天 性的自由。集團下屬動物實驗室均已取得《實驗動物使用許可證》,且每年均順利通過許可證 年檢及動物福利專項審查。

section: 2.4.1.4 供應商風險管理 / · 資質要求
text: 本集團在准入階段即開展系統性風險識別,重點關注財務穩定性、生產供貨能力、質量工藝水 平及行業信譽。本集團制定《供應商管理制度》,明確原輔料供應商原則上控制在2-3家,以 保障供貨的穩定性。若出現單一供應商的情況,公司將依據《變更管理制度》及《供應商管理 制度》啟動新增供應商流程,開展相應的質量研究工作,並按法規要求完成藥監部門報備後, 將其納入合格供應商清單,從而消除單一供應商帶來的風險。

table_cells.text: 影響描述 潛在財務影響
政策與法 規風險 碳定價上升
中游-行政與生產 下游-運輸與銷售
• 隨著碳定價機制和碳排放約束逐步強化，公 司能源使用及碳排放相關成本可能上升，從 而對整體運營成本和盈利能力產生影響。 • 物流運輸行業可能因碳定價機制面臨更高的 運營成本，這些成本上升可能部分由上游企
• 持續開展碳盤查，識別排放來 源與潛在減排點。 • 穩步推進生產基地的節能減排 項目以降低整體碳排放基數。 • 優先選擇低碳排放的物流服務 供應商。
中游-行政與生產 • 環境保護和氣候相關法規日趨嚴格，可能對 公司在排放控制、能源使用及信息披露方面 提出更高合規要求，增加管理和合規成本。
• 密切追蹤法規動態，規範內部 數據收集流程，確保信息披露 合規透明。
• 隨著客戶和醫療機構對低碳和可持續發展的 關注度提升，若公司在環境和氣候表現方面 未能滿足相關期望，可能對市場競爭力產生 不利影響。
• 積極推動價值鏈低碳轉型，探 索採用可再生或可重複利用的 綠色醫藥包裝材料。
上游-原材料採購 • 氣候變化及相關政策可能導致能源、化工原 料及包裝材料價格波動或上漲，從而增加原 材料採購成本。
• 建立靈活的戰略庫存，拓寬低 碳化工及包材的採購渠道。
• 若公司在氣候變化應對和環境管理方面的表 現未達到利益相關方預期，可能對品牌形象 和社會聲譽造成不利影響。
• 融資成本增加、營業收入 減少
• 建立完善的氣候變化治理架 構，通過高質量的披露向資本 市場展示降碳決心與成效。
• 向低碳或新技術轉型過程中，若新技術應用 不成熟或不匹配生產需求，可能對生產穩定 性、產品質量或成本控制帶來不確定性。
• 資本開支增加、營業成本 增加
• 在關鍵製藥工藝應用新技術前 進行充分驗證；優先選擇性能 穩定、經過同行驗證的成熟節 能設備。

text: 本集團位於哈爾濱和呼和浩特的運營場所在各情景及時間段下均面臨較高的極寒天氣風險,其 餘地點極寒天氣風險較低。另外,評估結果顯示本集團各運營地在SSP5-8.5情景下極寒天氣 的頻率和強度有所下降。 面對中長期的政策不確定性,本集團將化被動為主動,穩步推進全鏈路的減碳工作,並積極把 握向低碳經濟轉型機遇。本集團預期將穩步推進生產基地的節能降耗改造、探索可再生能源與 環保包裝的應用,在有效對沖長期能源與合規成本上漲風險的同時,提升供應鏈整體韌性。

text:
類型 | 具體舉措
項目合規管控 | • 項目選址嚴格遵守生態保護紅線等規劃要求,禁止位於自然保護區等敏感區。化學原 料藥等項目均建於合規產業園。
生態調查保護 | • 規劃初期識別並保護原生植被、水源地及關鍵物種棲息地。施工中採取樹木移植、設 置緩衝帶等措施。
豐富園區綠化 | • 廠區綠化採用「喬木+灌木+草本」多層次配置,種植多種植物以構建多樣化生態 環境。
可持續養護 | • 聘請專業團隊進行生態友好型養護,每年開展土壤監測,並制定極端天氣等生態應急 預案。
污染控制 | • 對項目產生的廢氣、廢水、噪聲、固廢等均採取嚴格治理措施,確保達標排放。

4.2 人才發展 / 表：人才引進項目
[Content]
集團致力於為每一位員工提供清晰、多元的成長路徑,通過縱橫交錯、多通道並行的職業發展 體系,支持員工在專業深度與管理廣度上持續發展,實現個人價值與組織目標的共同成長。我 們希望通過多維度、可選擇的發展路徑,確保各類人才都能在集團內部找到符合自身期望的成 長空間,實現人盡其才。

section: 4.2 人才發展 / 表：人才引進項目
text:
校園招聘 | • 作為人才儲備的核心項目,每年定期走進全國重點高校,通過舉辦宣講會、參與雙 選會等形式,與高校學子建立緊密聯繫,吸引並選拔具備潛力的畢業生加入。
社會招聘 | • 通過主流招聘平台(如前程無憂、智聯招聘、獵聘網等)持續發佈職位,確保信息 觸達的公平性,覆蓋擁有行業經驗的專業人才,滿足我們對成熟人才的即時需求。
內部推薦 | • 推行《優秀人才推薦獎勵辦法》,設立覆蓋全崗位的內部推薦獎勵機制,鼓勵員工 成為「人才發現官」,營造人人關注人才、舉薦人才的良好組織氛圍。
內部競聘 | • 遵循《內部競聘管理辦法》,開放內部崗位競聘機會,為現有員工提供清晰的職業 發展通道和橫向流動機會,優先從內部選拔人才,激發組織活力。
新媒體平台 | • 積極運營「石藥集團招聘在線」等官方新媒體平台,及時發佈招聘資訊、展示企業 文化與員工風貌,以更生動、直接的方式吸引新生代及被動求職者的關注。

text: 截至2025 年底,集團在銷產品涉及品規數量持續增長,廣泛覆蓋全國31個省市。在市場滲 透方面,集團產品已覆蓋全國逾35,000家醫療機構,三級醫院覆蓋率保持在90%以上,二級 醫院覆蓋率超過70%。與此同時,集團積極響應國家關於改革完善基層藥品聯動管理機制的 號召,成立專項工作組深耕縣級及基層醫療市場,梳理並落實31個省份的准入政策,顯著提 升了慢性病與常見病藥物在基層的可及性。在全球化進程中,集團銷售網絡已覆蓋50餘個國 家,2025 年重點開拓了拉美、非洲、中東及東南亞等新興市場,通過參考當地經濟水平制定 合理的定價策略,讓石藥質優價廉的產品惠及全球更多患者。

text: 本集團持續加大研發投入,致力於提高藥物可及性,降低患者經濟負擔。針對技術門檻高、價 格昂貴的納米藥物,集團率先在國內研發成功紫杉醇白蛋白、兩性黴素B脂質體等產品,打 破國外壟斷。同時,集團支持仿製藥進入市場以提高藥物的可負擔性,積極推進仿製藥開發, 2025 年已有帕拉米韋注射液、瑞戈非尼片等9款仿製藥取得註冊批件,為滿足國內患者用藥 需求、助力國產藥物替代做出積極貢獻。

section: 表：六大領域在產在銷產品及研發管線
text: 石藥集團積極對接國家醫保及帶量採購政策,通過價格讓利與目錄准入,切實減輕患者的經濟負擔和醫保基金的支付壓力。2025年,公司在醫保、集採、衛生方面,使藥品更可及到患者。 本集團致力於為廣大患者提供價格合理的藥品,充分考慮當地經濟發展水平和患者支付能力。 2025 年,本集團已制定並公開掛網《公平定價政策》,規範產品定價行為。面向當地普通民 眾,綜合考慮同類藥品市場價格、當地監管、當地消費水平等因素進行定價,不僅使石藥集團 的產品惠及面更加廣泛,也對當地病患提供優質、高效、經濟的用藥選擇。

section: 基藥
text:
仿製藥產品銷售 | • 向中低收入國家銷售阿莫西林膠囊、注射用頭孢曲松鈉、氨苄西林膠囊、注射用 普魯卡因青黴素強化鈉、注射用青黴素鈉、注射用美羅培南、阿奇黴素薄膜衣片 等多款產品,提升患者醫藥可及性。
藥物警戒系統建設 | • 本集團建立了完善的境外藥品不良反應監測與上報機制。當在境外發生不良反應 時,我們會協同當地代理與客戶,按當地規定向所在地監管機構報告,並同步通 知其他銷售同批產品的客戶進行上報。對於境外發生的嚴重不良反應,我們確保 在獲知後15日內向國家藥品不良反應監測中心報告;若藥品在境外因不良反應 被暫停銷售、使用或撤市,我們將在24小時內向國家藥品監督管理局及國家藥 品不良反應監測中心提交書面報告。所有其他不良反應信息均納入藥品定期安全 性更新報告體系。
醫務人員培訓 | • 本集團積極派遣人員指導當地醫務人員,並定期組織專家進行現場交流與培訓, 以持續強化當地的用藥安全體系。2025年,本集團組織中國和東南亞各國醫院交 流9次,過向境外醫生介紹TNK優勢、使用方法,以及向東南亞各國專家傳遞 NBP、TNK產品信息。

section: 5.3.4 大病患者關愛 / 案例：「困境患者醫療救助」項目
text: 作為石藥集團踐行「健康中國」戰略的核心平台,石藥普恩基金會在重特大疾病救助領域一直 在參與慈善救助,基金會開展的針對低保、特困、低收入家庭、因病致貧等患大病患者的「困 境腫瘤大病援助」項目、「困境患者醫療救助」項目、「患者援助」項目,進一步踐行了「健 康中國」發展戰略。在以上重特大疾病醫療救助領域,2025年,本集團累計投入捐贈藥品 23.5 萬盒,救助人次達104,590 人次。

section: 5.3.4 大病患者關愛 / 案例：「困境患者醫療救助」項目
text: 面對先天性心臟病(如房間隔缺損、室間隔缺損、 動脈導管未閉、肺動脈狹窄)及後天性心臟病(如 冠心病、高血壓性心臟病、風濕性心臟病)帶來的 嚴峻挑戰,許多困難家庭在求醫路上步履維艱。為 緩解這一困境,本集團「困境患者醫療救助項目」 於2024 年正式啟動,旨在為生命續航,為每一顆 亟待救治的心臟賦予希望。2025年,該項目支出 94.72 萬元,開展 30 場患者救助關懷活動,幫扶困 境患者 90 人,志願服務時間達 1,290 小時。
